text:
Artturi Lehkonen has 15 goals in 21 games, and he got two points against his first NHL team on Nov. 14 as Colorado beat Montreal without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar, per TSN. The Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal wrote that he is now on the top line and the top penalty kill unit.

The role is real. The scoring rate is not, at least not all of it. He has 15 goals on 8.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 33% after 14% last season, and the Avalanche have scored 9.0 more goals than expected with him on the ice. That is the strongest due to cool flag in this group: the chances are real, but that finishing rarely lasts.

Evolving-Hockey adds a caution from last season: he played with teammates in the 99th percentile by impact, which flatters raw on-ice numbers. At five on five this season his on-ice share of expected goals is 50.9%, a little below the team without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a signature: 27% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward.
